items.title: Governing the Privacy-Personalization Tension in AI-Driven Marketing Platforms: An Integrative Framework for Customer Data Platforms
items.abstract: Customer data platforms (CDPs) are increasingly positioned as the data and decision infrastructure of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven marketing. Yet the academic literature has not adequately explained when a CDP can reconcile privacy compliance with hyper-personalization, nor how this reconciliation depends on platform governance, consumer trust, data quality, and responsible AI controls. This article develops an integrative conceptual framework through a structured interdisciplinary literature review. The review covers marketing, information systems, platform studies, consumer behavior, data governance, privacy engineering, and AI ethics. A structured integrative review with a systematic search component and concept-centric synthesis produced a final analytical corpus of 70 sources, comprising 60 peer-reviewed publications, one book, eight authoritative legal, policy, or standards documents, and one industry source used only for descriptive context. The synthesis identifies CDP governance capabilities as the central antecedent of two complementary mechanisms: privacy assurance and customer-data quality. Privacy assurance strengthens consumer trust and willingness to disclose first- and zero-party data, while governed identity resolution, provenance, interoperability, and data minimization improve the reliability of inputs available to machine learning, recommendation systems, generative AI, and autonomous agents. The resulting personalization effectiveness influences customer and marketing outcomes, but the relationships are conditional on responsible AI controls, platform ecosystem governance, regulatory intensity, data sensitivity, consumer privacy orientation, and organizational maturity. Seven direct-effect propositions and a decomposed family of path-specific moderation and boundary propositions specify theoretically expected relationships without implying causal identification by the review itself. The article contributes by conceptualizing the CDP not as a neutral database or stand-alone compliance tool, but as a governed platform control plane that coordinates data rights, AI decisioning, and multi-actor accountability. The framework offers a research agenda and practical design principles for privacy-preserving, transparent, and accountable AI-driven marketing ecosystems.

items.title: Healthy skepticism in AI: a data visualization research agenda
items.abstract: Research in data visualization of artificial intelligence (AI) models has historically focused on enhancing trust through visual explanations of AI. The trustworthiness line of work was built at least partially on an assumption that humans were critical users unlikely to adopt AI technology. It is increasingly clear that human trust levels in AI span, in fact, a wide range from critical to over-reliant. There is an urgent need to support both trust and healthy skepticism in AI solutions. We argue that it is healthy for humans to adopt a skeptical view both on the results of AI models and on the use of such AI models. We share our thoughts on the rising phenomenon of over-reliance on AI models, the risks and opportunities in using AI models, and the role of data visualization in over-reliance situations where humans are not motivated to engage in critical thinking.

items.title: How Agent-Driven Creative Trace Mining Reshapes Design Behavior in a Deployment Study of Intent-Aligned Multimodal Design
items.abstract: Designers continuously capture inspirations across media, yet these creative traces remain underutilized in computational design support. We present DesignJournal, an agent-driven system that mines multimodal creative traces and transforms them into intent-aligned image generation. The system consolidates artifacts into a unified workspace and employs an agentic pipeline for structured grouping, belief-guided prompt refinement, and iterative intent updates. We developed a framework that classifies sequential design actions, deriving a hierarchical action taxonomy from interaction logs. We used it to examine how agent affordances reshape design behavior. A 10-day deployment study with eight professional designers compared baseline and agent-supported conditions across 5838 classified actions. Agent support significantly reduced the frequency of spatial repositioning actions, particularly small-distance movements, while sequential transition structures shifted from extended repositioning chains toward relational encoding sequences. Awareness of agent interpretation shaped upstream recording behavior, and agent-mediated collaboration extended designers’ creative reach beyond independent exploration.

items.title: How Do Users Negotiate Harmful Value Conflicts with AI Companions? A Study with Minion, a Technology Probe for In-Situ Human–AI Conflict Response
items.abstract: AI companions increasingly sustain long-term, emotionally engaging relationships but can also make discriminatory remarks or exert control, leaving users to manage harmful conflicts. We analyze 146 posts describing harmful value conflicts with AI companions, then use Minion, a technology probe offering response suggestions ranging from persuasion to boundary setting, to study how 22 users negotiate scenario-based conflicts over one week. We find that participants combine softer and harder strategies. Conflicts involving the values of Universalism and Tradition are especially difficult to negotiate, particularly when reinforced by AI personas or platform constraints. items.title: How does AI-generated assessment compare to expert assessment in simulation-based experiences: Analyzing AI-human interrater reliability
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In the health professions, artificial intelligence simulation-based experiences (AI-SBEs) are increasingly used to evaluate learner performance and provide feedback. Benefits of AI-SBEs include providing instantaneous feedback, allowing more practice opportunities than feasible using traditional methods, and reducing educator burden. However, methods for calibrating AI feedback are underdeveloped. METHODS: This study evaluated the feedback provided by a generative AI-based software program (SimConverse) when assessing simulated patient interactions using the Weight Sensitivity Instrument (WSI), a checklist used to assess learners' weight bias-related clinical behaviors. A two-phase interrater reliability (IRR) approach was used. First, iterative prompt engineering was guided by AI-human IRR results. Four authors and four volunteers generated 31 interactions in SimConverse. Interaction transcripts were downloaded, and another author with expertise in the WSI manually reviewed and scored the transcripts. Percent agreement and Gwet's AC1 were calculated to compare AI and expert assessments, and the research team reviewed feedback statements and agreement statistics to identify rubric instructions in need of revision. After revising the rubric in SimConverse, four authors produced 10 additional SBE interactions. Expert and AI assessments were explored. In phase two, the AI-SBE was piloted with 60 medical students in a larger intervention study. A random sample of 30 student transcripts were assessed for AI-human IRR, and students' comments about the AI-SBE were reviewed. RESULTS: Of the 11 WSI items, expert and AI agreement was consistently good or very good for 7 items across all rounds (Gwet's AC1=0.71 and higher). One item initially showed poor agreement (Gwet's AC1=0.56), but agreement improved after prompt engineering (final Gwet's AC1=0.89). The improved item assessed whether students made specific statements (asked if weight loss was a priority). Three other items had persistent poor agreement (final Gwet's AC1=0.42, 0.66, 0.64). These items required broader contextual assessment of the transcripts. Most open-ended student reactions to the AI-SBE were positive. CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that AI scoring and feedback within AI-SBEs requires iterative prompt engineering and educator/researcher guidance. Tuning was more successful for content-specific items than context-dependent items. Future work could explore best practices for prompt refinement, particularly for more complex and context-dependent rubric items.

items.title: Human-AI Conversational Behaviors Predict Unassisted Task Performance
items.abstract: Assistance from AI tools has supported and improved human performance across domains. However, recent research suggests that these immediate benefits may entail future costs, including diminished performance when AI assistance is no longer available. We study how human-AI interaction behaviors correlate with immediate and future unassisted task performance across two game-based problem-solving user studies ($n=139$ and $n=111$), using a \textit{dialogue act} framework adopted from a tutor-student dialogue taxonomy. In our studies, verbalizing thought processes correlates with higher unassisted outcomes, whereas directly requesting solutions correlates negatively. Similar to these participant-side patterns, assistant explanations of the current problem state are associated with better subsequent unassisted performance, whereas directly providing the next action is associated with worse performance. Qualitative and subtype analyses further show that ostensibly similar reasoning turns can elicit different assistance. Our findings suggest that preserving users' cognitive participation in problem-solving may support performance beyond AI-assisted interaction.

items.title: Implementation of OHS Internal Audit as Hazard Control at Semarang Container Terminal
items.abstract: The rapid growth of global maritime trade has increased the risk of occupational accidents at container terminals, necessitating a strong Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) system. This study aims to examine the relationship between the implementation of internal OHS audits, communication patterns, and hazard control at container terminals in Semarang City. Using a qualitative descriptive method with a case study approach, this research seeks to gain an in-depth understanding of the interplay among internal audits, communication, and hazard control. Data were collected through method triangulation, including in depth interviews, field observations, and document analysis, involving HSE staff, internal auditors, supervisors, and auditees. Data analysis was conducted using ATLAS.ti software through open coding, axial coding, and selective coding stages. The findings reveal that systematic internal audits, supported by integrated digital communication systems and structured discussion forums, significantly contribute to hazard control and worker compliance. The integration of audit processes and communication fosters a safety-oriented work culture and accelerates audit resolution. This study concludes that the synergy between routine audits and effective communication enhances the effectiveness of hazard control programs. The research contributes to OHS literature by presenting a comprehensive model integrating audit practices, communication strategies, and hazard control mechanisms.

items.title: Intelligent Mechatronics: intelligence in the design process, not only the machine
items.abstract: Designing a physical machine requires mechanical, electronic, control, and software decisions to be settled together, each constraining the others, under the standards governing the environment it will work in. This reasoning is held by experienced engineers and rarely written down. That, I argue, is why artificial intelligence has reached the design of software but not of the machines that software runs on. Physical design is, in part, genuinely harder, and its errors are costly and irreversible, but that is not the whole explanation. Software’s design reasoning was written down alongside the public code that an AI could learn from; the knowledge that conceives and sizes a physical system was not. As the design bottleneck shifts to physical systems, intelligence must be applied to the design process itself, not only to the product. Taking mechatronics as the case, I find that where its defining sources invoke intelligence at all, it is for the product or the discipline that builds it, never for the process that designs it. The capture of tacit, cross-domain design knowledge in a form that AI can use is a binding constraint on AI-assisted physical design, and the most neglected as well. A three-layer model locates it: Layer 1, this design knowledge is the missing foundation; the AI reasoning and agent layers above advance rapidly but cannot design physical systems without it. The physical machine and its intelligent twin are developed together from this foundation. A worked design-rationale analysis of an offshore-crane actuation decision grounds what Layer 1 must hold: the rationale residue that existing formats do not capture. In this article, I set out a research agenda, from capturing this knowledge to generalizing beyond mechatronics, and state the conditions under which its central claim would fail.

items.title: Leadership, resilience and safety outcomes: A study of Indian construction workers post-COVID-19
items.abstract: Worker safety remains a serious concern for the Indian construction industry, where unsafe worker behaviour is a key contributor to workplace accidents, and leadership has a strong impact on safety behaviour. Construction industry researchers have largely focused on how leadership styles and safety climate affect employees' overall satisfaction. Prior research suggests that the quality of the association between leaders and followers may relate to followers' resilience. Leader–member exchange (LMX) captures this relationship quality, defined by trust, mutual respect, support and role clarity between supervisors and workers. While earlier studies have generally treated LMX as a single, uniform construct, this study advances the literature by unpacking its four distinct sub-dimensions to better understand how each uniquely contributes to worker outcomes. By linking these sub-dimensions to resilience and safety behaviour amongst Indian construction workers in the post-coronavirus disease 2019 environment, this study offers a richer theoretical explanation and contextually relevant insights for strengthening leadership practices and safety management in high-risk settings. To reduce unsafe behaviour amongst construction workers, this study examined how the four sub-dimensions of LMX relate to employee resilience and safety behaviour. Hypothesised relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling, with data collected from 139 construction workers across various construction companies in the Delhi/National Capital Region using purposive sampling. Results show a positive association between all four LMX dimensions: affect, contribution, loyalty and professional respect, and employee resilience. Additionally, employees' capability to cope with adverse situations enhances their safety behaviour, indicating that despite pandemic-related challenges, leaders' support, emotional connection, mutual goal setting and inspirational motivation helped employees overcome adversity, fostering intrinsic motivation to abide by safety norms and engage actively in safety behaviour.

items.title: Machine Deliberation as an Organisational Resource: Toward a Theory of Cognitive Capacity Governance
items.abstract: Organisations have begun to purchase reasoning the way they long purchased electricity: metered, priced per unit and elastic on demand. Large language models sold through per-token interfaces let a firm dial the depth of machine deliberation applied to any problem, from a shallow single pass to prolonged multi-step reasoning, at a price that scales with depth. Management theory is unprepared for this. Its foundational treatments assume cognition is scarce because human attention is scarce, and its resource theories treat computational capacity as background infrastructure rather than as a governed input to advantage. This conceptual paper introduces the construct of governed cognitive capacity, defined as an organisation's metered stock of machine deliberation together with the routines that shape its demand, allocate its depth and assure its outputs. Drawing from resource orchestration, the attention-based view, bounded rationality and the emerging literatures on delegation to agentic artefacts, six propositions are developed linking capacity governance to value capture, including an inverted-U relation between deliberation depth and net value conditional on output verifiability, an allocation-not-access locus of competitive advantage and a transaction-cost boundary for external agent services. A three-plane governance framework - demand shaping, allocation and assurance - organises the propositions for practice. Contributions to theory, implications for managers and an operationalisation agenda are discussed.

items.title: Methods and Practices Supporting Tacit Knowledge Mobilisation in Continuous Improvement: A Rapid Review
items.abstract: Aim: The aim of this article was to identify current research directions concerning the methods and practices for mobilising tacit knowledge in continuous improvement (CI) processes. Methodology: The article is based on a systematic literature review using the rapid review format. The review was conducted using the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus and EBSCO databases. A search strategy based on three conceptual blocks related to continuous improvement, tacit knowledge, and methods and practices for mobilising tacit knowledge was employed. A total of 67 articles meeting the criteria were identified. After deduplication and screening, 20 publications qualified for full-text assessment, and 14 papers were included in the final analysis and synthesis. Results: Research has shown that the mobilisation of tacit knowledge in CI is most often understood as a process embedded in work practice and requiring direct engagement with actual work processes. The literature abounds with methods for eliciting tacit knowledge based on observation and action learning, interviews, workshops, and reflective meetings, as well as organizational practices for knowledge transfer and tools for knowledge externalisation and codification. The analysis also highlighted examples of modern digital solutions supporting the externalisation and transfer of tacit knowledge in improvement processes, including elements of artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual reality (VR). Implications and recommendations: Further research is needed to assess the relative effectiveness of methods for eliciting tacit knowledge and to explore how the AI and VR-based solutions can improve the externalisation of tacit knowledge in organizational practice. Originality/value: This article organizes the fragmented findings from the continuous improvement field related to the mobilisation of tacit knowledge, presenting a synthetic overview of the methods, practices, and boundary conditions for its mobilisation in CI from 2015 to 2025. By synthesizing diverse research perspectives, the article contributes to a better understanding of the mechanisms of tacit knowledge mobilisation, including its elicitation, transfer, externalisation, and codification, in the context of continuous improvement processes.

items.title: MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents
items.abstract: Training and evaluating interactive language agents typically requires rich user interactions, yet collecting human feedback is expensive and difficult to scale. Simulated users offer a scalable alternative, but they must both resemble real user behavior and provide useful learning experiences for agents. In contrast, most agent-training frameworks rely on off-the-shelf assistant LLMs, whose helpfulness can make them overly cooperative, explicit, and behaviorally homogeneous compared with real users. We introduce MIMESIS, a purpose-built user simulator trained on human conversations with explicit reasoning supervision and 13 realistic behavioral patterns derived from real user interactions. Empirically, our 9B model achieves a SOUL-Index of 65.7, surpassing the strongest frontier model. Compared with Claude-Opus-5, the strongest baseline on RealUserSim and SimulatorArena, MIMESIS improves behavioral fidelity by 13.4 points and reduces Turing distance by 3.6 points, respectively. We then freeze the simulator and train an agent by interacting with the frozen simulator using multi-turn reinforcement learning. Across eight environments, training with MIMESIS yields better agent performance than training with GPT-5.5 under all nine unseen user simulators, demonstrating stronger generalization to new user simulators. Moreover, we propose Coached On-Policy Self-Distillation (CSD), which leverages simulator-generated private reasoning traces and subsequent utterances as feedback on how well the agent addresses user needs. A coach converts this information into concise coaching notes that describe how the agent can better anticipate user needs and adapt its behavior over the course of an interaction. CSD turns this feedback into dense, token-level supervision beyond sparse task rewards, yielding further gains across all nine evaluation user models.

items.title: Motivación y elección profesional en estudiantes universitarios desde la teoría de la autodeterminación
items.abstract: Background: Motivation is one of the factors that influences not only the choice of a career path but also the ability to remain in it despite social, economic, academic, or personal difficulties. Objective: To understand the underlying motivations in career choice through Self-Determination Theory (SDT) proposed by Deci and Ryan. Methodology: The research approach was qualitative with a phenomenological design. The unit of analysis consisted of 11 students selected through purposive sampling. The data collection technique was in-depth, semi-structured interviews. Results: The findings reveal the prevalence of intrinsic motivation. Regarding the basic psychological needs of competence and relatedness, there is a positive appreciation for becoming better psychology professionals. Conclusion: Motivation for career choice strengthens over time within a process of meaning-making guided by SDT, which not only sustains academic interest but also fosters a commitment to the quality of the future professional.

items.title: Perceived Organizational Support and Self-Efficacy as Drivers of Employee Performance: A Moderated Mediation Model of Employee Engagement and Organizational Commitment
items.abstract: This study aims to examine the associations of perceived organizational support and self-efficacy with employee performance, with employee engagement as a mediating mechanism and organizational commitment as a moderator of the employee engagement–performance relationship. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 255 employees working in R&D and supporting functions within the electronics manufacturing industry in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results showed that perceived organizational support and self-efficacy were not significantly associated with employee performance directly, whereas both were positively and significantly associated with employee engagement. Employee engagement was positively and significantly associated with employee performance and significantly mediated the relationships of perceived organizational support and self-efficacy with performance. Organizational commitment did not significantly moderate the employee engagement–performance relationship. These findings indicate that organizational and personal resources are linked to performance primarily through employee engagement, underscoring engagement as a central explanatory mechanism. However, the cross-sectional design precludes causal and temporal inference, and reverse or reciprocal relationships cannot be excluded. Future longitudinal or experimental studies should test the temporal ordering of these relationships and examine whether alternative organizational conditions strengthen the engagement–performance link. Managerially, the findings support practices that foster engagement through supervisor support, recognition, autonomy, coaching, and meaningful work design.
